<p class="hero-affiliation">School of Psychological Sciences · Te Herenga Waka — Victoria University of Wellington</p>
<h1 class="hero-title">OTTO <em>Lab</em></h1>
<p class="hero-descriptor">Observational Target Trial Operations</p>

<p class="hero-lede">How can investigators estimate causal effects in psychology when experiments are impractical or unethical? Investigators can rarely assign people at random to attend religious services or to work longer hours. At OTTO Lab, we develop and apply methods for estimating causal effects from observational data. We specify the randomised trial we would run if we could, the <em>target trial</em>, then emulate that trial with longitudinal studies such as the New Zealand Attitudes and Values Study.</p>
<div class="hero-actions">
<a href="research.qmd" class="btn btn-primary">Research</a>
<a href="resources.qmd" class="btn btn-secondary">Resources</a>
<a href="mailto:joseph.bulbulia@vuw.ac.nz" class="btn btn-secondary">Email Joseph Bulbulia</a>
</div>
<p class="hero-text">An estimate from observational data has a causal interpretation only under assumptions, chiefly that the baseline measures we adjust for account for all common causes of treatment and outcome. In each study, we state these assumptions and assess how far our conclusions depend on them.</p>

## `religionmap.org`

[`religionmap.org`](https://religionmap.org/) maps places of worship worldwide for reproducible spatial and cultural analysis.

[Visit `religionmap.org`](https://religionmap.org/) · [Code](https://github.com/go-bayes/places-of-worship)

## Collaboration and teaching

We supervise graduate students, teach methods for causal inference, and collaborate with investigators in New Zealand and internationally. We also build software, including the [`margot`](resources.qmd#r-packages) R package. To discuss supervision or collaboration, email Joseph Bulbulia at [joseph.bulbulia@vuw.ac.nz](mailto:joseph.bulbulia@vuw.ac.nz).
